title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Ensure that `prev_mask` is always protected
description:
Closes https://github.com/tidyverse/dplyr/issues/6207

The most minimal reprex I could come up with to show this issue was:

```r
library(magrittr)

var <- "x"
data <- data.frame(feature = letters[1:10], imp = 1:10)

gctorture2(5L)

for (kk in 1:100) {
  cat(sprintf("Run #%d\n", kk))
  
  data.frame(feature = letters[1:10]) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(data, by = "feature") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(!!var := 1.0)
}

cat("Done\n")
```

Which would often error with:

```r
Error in dplyr::mutate(., `:=`(!!var, 1)) : 
   'rho' must be an environment not promise: detected in C-level eval
```

This only happened when there were >=2 pipes in a pipe chain, and didn't happen at all when the pipes were removed. We also had to be very aggressive with `gctorture2()` to get it to show up at all, so it was probably very rare.

It turns out that as we are updating `prev_mask` and moving from one iteration of the `while` loop to the next, there is a very short window where `prev_mask` is unprotected and can be gc'd. On the second iteration of the `while` loop, right after `REPROTECT(mask, mask_pi);` the `prev_mask` becomes unprotected. The first line of `r_env_bind_lazy()` runs an allocating function, which is when it is possible for `prev_mask` to become gc'd. You can force this to happen reliably by placing `R_gc();` right after the `REPROTECT(mask, mask_pi);` line and running the reprex above.

title: Make testthat tests conditional on its presence.
description:
`magrittr` fails tests on CRAN in winUCRT because `testthat` is missing.
`testthat` is a suggested package.

This creates a huge cascade of failures of packages that depend on `magrittr`.

`magrittr` should be able to pass tests on CRAN with no ERRORs even
if suggested packages are missing.

This PR reduces the `magrittr` problems to a NOTE about `testthat`
being missing.

title: rm tab character from debug_pipe.R
description: There was a presumably accidental tab character there. Why does it matter? I'm about to apply a [`pkgstats` package](https://github.com/mpadge/pkgstats) to the entire historical CRAN archive, for which `magrittr` is used as a conveniently small demo package. The analyses are largely derived from outputs of both [`ctags`](https://ctags.io) and [`gtags`](https://www.gnu.org/software/global/), but tab characters mess with these outputs, and can lead to errors when attempting to automatically analyse code.

title: Fix visibility forwarding of `%$%` on old R versions
description:
By making it follow the lazy path. Closes #226. It failed because the eager code path cleans up `.`. On older R versions, this calls back into the R-level `rm()` function which returns invisibly. On 4.0 there was no issue because we delete the binding with the new C-level API. This is worked around by following the lazy path which is more appropriate anyway.

Also make lazy the other pipes `%T>` and `%<>%`.

title: Review tradeoffs vignette
description:
Branched from #218.

Compares the properties different implementations of the pipe with a focus on three variants:

- `pipe_nested()`, the code transformation approach that will likely be used in a future R version.
- `pipe_eager_lexical()` implemented in #217.
- `pipe_lazy_masking()` implemented in #218, and which is the tentative new behaviour for `%>%`.

title: Switch to lazy implementation
description:
Branched from #216.

Adds named variants `pipe_eager_lexical()`, `pipe_lazy_masking()`, and `pipe_nested()` to easily experiment with the properties of three complementary pipe implementations.

Switch `%>%` to lazy evaluation in a mask, so that `stop("foo") %>% try()` works. No impact on reverse dependencies. This brings the pipe closer to the implementation that will likely be included in a future version of R.

Will be switched to lazy evaluation in a masking environment in an ulterior PR as the lazy property is more important than the lexical property.

title: Implement calling_env()
description:
This implements a helper function that makes it easy to retrieve the original environment that called a pipe chain. This will help magrittr-aware tools to reinforce the idiom that a pipe chain is one single function entity.

Another way of implementing this would be to climb the calling stack dynamically, looking for magrittr's anchors (`_fseq`, `_function_list`, etc). This way `calling_env()` would work when called in functions embedded deeply in pipe components. If we start from `n = 5`, there would be no cost when `calling_env()` is called from the top level of a pipe component. But I suspect it may get very costly if called outside of a pipe chain and the calling stack is large.

title: Convert fseq to function
description:
Example:

```
> as.function(. %>% rexp(n=10) %>% sort)
function (.) 
{
    . <- rexp(., n = 10)
    sort(.)
}
```

This gives much shorter call stacks and better error messages. Example with `options(error = expression(traceback(1)))`:

```
> 5 %>% runif %>% paste(collapse=" ") %>% stop
Error in magrittr(.) : 
  0.668534632306546 0.386715253116563 0.194241847842932 0.261686375364661 0.222338400548324
3: stop(.)
2: magrittr(.) at pipe.R#39
1: 5 %>% runif %>% paste(collapse = " ") %>% stop
```

Another advantage is that visibility is handled implicitly.

~~Calling an fseq still uses `freduce()`. I think we can get rid of `freduce()` entirely, and implement the fseq as a function right away. This requires some more work, we should discuss first.~~

A functional sequence is now a plain old function with class `fseq` and an attribute `magrittr:function_list` that holds the list of functions (previously `env[["_function_list"]]`). The `env` with all the underscore-prefixed variables has gone. I think this simplifies things a lot.

All tests pass locally. Closes #107, which adds more tests and is included here. Also added documentation stub in vignette.

The idea is stolen from [vadr](http://github.com/crowding/vadr)'s `mkchain()` function; the implementation is mine.

CC @crowding, @gaborcsardi.

Related: #94, #95

Probably breaks #70

title: Add or_default operator
description:
Hi,

I created an operator to assign default values to variables. Maybe this is useful to others. I don´t quite know if magrittr is the right place [1] but I am happy to hear feedback. Essentially it ports the notation from javascript `var x = y || 0;`  to R `x <- y %||% 0`.

It is currently implemented to fallback to the default value if the first value is NA (or vector of NA) or NULL. It could be used in the following ways:

``` R
my_function <- function(x) {
 y <- x %||% 1
 100 / y
}
```

``` R
data.frame(x = c(NA, 1, NA, NA, 2)) %>%
 mutate(y = x %||% 0)
```

Maybe this has all been done before - I don´t know :)

Another problem is that RCHECK does not accept "|" in the name of a function it seems. I also called it "or_default", but maybe there is a proper name for it. In addition, this operator would probably still need some more work to cover all use cases.

Greetings
Dirk

title: Tamper: pipe-friendly version of utils::recover()
description:
## Comments

First of all, this is not ready yet. Just wanted to know what you think about it. If you don't like it in `magrittr`, it will be perfectly fine in another package.

Second, this is joint work with @krlmlr. Actually, we worked it out right after a useR! pub night, between 1am and 3am. :) 
## Motivation

As much as we like the pipes, because of the NSE and the long stack, it is sometimes really hard to find where exactly the error is. So the idea of `tamper` is that it knows how `magrittr` works, and helps you find where to look. 
## Example

This is actually an easy example, but hopefully will do for a start. If you set `options(error = tamper)` and then run the following:

``` r
  1:10 %>%
    (function(x) force(x)) %>%
    multiply_by(10) %>%
    add(10) %>%
    add("oh no!") %>%
    subtract(5) %>%
    divide_by(5)
```

then you'll see something like this:

``` r
Error in add(., "oh no!") : non-numeric argument to binary operator

Enter a pipe stage number, 1 to switch mode, or 0 to exit   

1: Show full stack frames

2:    1:10 %>%
3:      (function (x) 
         force(x))(.) %>%
4:      multiply_by(., 10) %>%
5:      add(., 10) %>%
6: ->   add(., "oh no!") %>%
7:      subtract(., 5) %>%
8:      divide_by(., 5) 

Selection: 
```
- The stage in which the error happened is marked with an arrow.
- You can go to that stage and save the temporary value from the pipe (we could also have a menu for this, actually.)
- You can switch to the full stack trace (and back to this view).
## Possible improvements
- ~~Mark the pipe stages on the full stack trace as well.~~ **I decided not to, for now.**
- ~~Currently only the innermost pipeline is shown, we could probably do better.~~ **I decided not to, for now.**
- ~~Have a non-interactive version, like `dump.frames()`. This will be also easier to test.~~
- ~~Get rid of the `pryr` dependency, maybe.~~
- Write real test cases. (How?)

title: Bruyere
description:
Main differences in "bruyere" and "master" are 
- Different handling of LHS. 
  - If possible, evaluation will happen as in master, but with `__LHS` replaced by `<the expresson>`. This will preserve the call, which gives better behavior e.g. using formula interfaced functions (lm, glm, etc), and when the call is used to generate labels, e.g. in plot.
  - If the above is not possible, which happens when lhs cannot be treated as a call or name, then `__LHS` is used as name in the evaluation of the lhs. An example is `iris %>% dplyr::filter(Species %>% substr(1, 1) == "v")`. The same is not the case if using `iris %>% subset(Species %>% substr(1, 1) == "v")`.
- Data manipulation/filtering functions have been removed to keep the aim and scope of magrittr very specific. Instead a variety of aliases have been added for operations such as multiplication, addition, etc.
- Examples in the readme have been updated to reflect the changes.

title: Add the functionality to memorize "temporal variable" to use it after chain evaluation
description:
Hi;
Thank you for your great package.
I'm really fascinated by your approach(and F#?).

I try to introduce the functionality to "memorize" temporal variable to use after the chain evaluation.
I think that it is very usefule when you chain data manipulation and visualization 
because processed data will be needed sometimes after chain evaluation.

For example, you can write like the following using "%->%" operator I made.

``` r
x <- 1:10
x %>% sum %->% y %>% multiply_by(10)
y
(output)
[1] 55
```

And as second example,

``` r
iris %>% group_by(Species) %>% summarise(mn=mean(Sepal.Length)) %->% res %>% qplot(data=.,x=Species,y=mn,geom="bar",stat="identity")
res
(output)
Source: local data frame [3 x 2]

     Species    mn
1     setosa 5.006
2 versicolor 5.936
3  virginica 6.588
```

Let me know what you think.
